sections.title: AI & the World
sections.brief: What AI progress changes for work, science, money, and ordinary life.
sections.prompt: Lead of the paper. Concrete AI progress and its effects on work, science, money, safety, and daily life. Decision-oriented: what a general reader should know or do. Two or three items.

sections.title: Comics
sections.brief: Today's general-audience strips, official links, and a few comics we can print.
sections.prompt: One or two original sentences on which general-audience strip is worth opening today. Do not describe copyrighted panels. Do not include image URLs. No political cartoons.

sections.title: AI editorial
sections.brief: An argument about AI, the multiverse, and mathematics.
sections.prompt: A short editorial on AI, the multiverse as a serious idea, and mathematics. Argumentative, sourced, and useful to someone deciding what to read next. Leave defender briefings to the security sections.

sections.title: Biology
sections.brief: CRISPR news and the public debate over designed life.
sections.prompt: New CRISPR news and the public conversation about designing biological systems from DNA, including ideas that do not start from a human genome. Explainer and legal or ethical framing only.

sections.title: Cancer
sections.brief: Treatment and research news, evidence-based, with no medical advice.
sections.prompt: Cancer treatment and research news for a general adult reader. Report what a study, trial, or review found, in plain language, and what is still uncertain. Evidence-based. No medical advice, no dosing, no personal treatment plans, and no named patients.

sections.title: Education
sections.brief: How AI is changing teaching and learning.
sections.prompt: How AI is being used in teaching and learning: classrooms, tutoring, assessment, and teacher workload. Say what the evidence supports. No product pitches and no stories about a named student.

sections.title: Narcolepsy & sleep
sections.brief: Sleep and narcolepsy, written for any reader.
sections.prompt: Narcolepsy and sleep, as a general explainer for any adult reader. Fully anonymous. No names, no personal history, and no reference to a publisher or a site.

sections.title: AI security
sections.prompt: AI security only: model abuse, data exposure, and defender checks at briefing level. No attack procedures. General cybersecurity belongs in its own section, not this one.

sections.title: Cybersecurity
sections.brief: Incidents, patches, and what a defender should check.
sections.prompt: Cybersecurity for a general reader and a defender: incidents, patches, and what to check. High level. No attack procedures and no payloads. Keep this separate from AI-only security.

sections.title: Protecting your company
sections.prompt: Generic enterprise security guidance any company could use. Never name or hint at a specific employer, workplace, product line, or industry in a way that would identify one organization.

sections.title: AI money-making
sections.brief: Legal ways people are using AI to earn.
sections.prompt: Practical, legal ways people are using AI to earn a living. No get-rich claims, no investment advice, and no schemes.

sections.title: Life improvement & thinking tools
sections.brief: Clearer thinking and ways to organize ordinary life.
sections.prompt: Tools and habits for thinking more clearly and organizing ordinary life. Short and usable. No lectures and no personal diary.

sections.title: Space & aliens
sections.brief: Space news, the search for life, and minds we are building.
sections.prompt: Space news and the scientific search for life. Include, when it fits, the idea that AI is a new kind of mind we are building, a sort of alien of our own making. Separate evidence from speculation.

sections.title: Weird side
sections.brief: Mysteries and odd stories, lightly held.
sections.prompt: Aliens, mysteries, and conspiracy theories as light curiosity. Friendly. Nothing anti-government, nothing partisan, nothing offensive. Label speculation as speculation.

sections.title: Big World News
sections.brief: Major developments a careful reader might otherwise miss.
sections.prompt: Cool major developments in technology, transport, science, and business. The kind of item a reader misses: a Tesla Cybercab milestone, a new Roadster, a shift in shipping, aviation, energy, or materials. Skip celebrity gossip and partisan politics.
